fixes.explanation: Dawn and the gate aren't in her plan, friend. Rahab says, “Hide yourselves there for three days until they have returned; then go on your way.” (Joshua 2:16) The searchers coming back is the signal, and no gate gets a vote. I think that's a plan you can set your oven timer by.

True. Rahab tells the spies that the fear of them has fallen on the people, “…so that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of you.” Picture a whole city with the same knot in its stomach. She says it straight to the spies on her roof, and her words cover everyone in the land.

Yes, family. She asks them to spare her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them. Rahab had just hidden two strangers, and now she asks for something for the people she loves. I think that tells you a lot about her heart. She also asks the spies for a sure sign, so she's asking for more than a quick promise.

Ai isn't on her map, friend. Rahab says, “Go to the hill country…” and the reason the text gives is simple: so their pursuers will not find them. One place, one reason, and no city in it. Picking the right hiding spot matters, and I'm told some stampers get stuck in a junk drawer with no say in it at all.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The claim that nobody was willing to admit their fear is unsupported. Rahab herself tells the spies about it.
The explanation claims that her family was the first thing Rahab thought about and gives her reason for wanting a sure sign. The passage does not state either.
The passage does not say Rahab avoided sending the spies to a city because the searchers would look there.
Papa says he hid in the drawer, implying he chose it as a hiding place. His backstory says he was put there.
